title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing/fairness/starvation prevention and timeouts
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to improve fairness and prevent starvation; added per-queue timeouts and observability; default behavior is backward-compatible; gradual rollout described in PR body.
description: Motivation: customers and internal canaries have observed tail latency and occasional request starvation under high multiplexing when model sequence-length distributions vary across tenants. This patch tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce queueing tail, enforce fairness across priority queues, and add configurable per-request timeouts and elastic dequeue heuristics. Changes include: 1) Introduce a dual-queue scheduler with age-priority promotion and a soft-deadline eviction for long-waiting items; 2) Add per-queue dynamic weight adjustments based on observed throughput and recent wait-time distributions to avoid starvation when a low-throughput tenant is competing with high-throughput tenants; 3) Implement a dequeue timeout metric and a request-level soft timeout (configurable) that triggers early fallback to lower-cost model variants or immediate short-path inference; 4) Add a delayed-batch admission heuristic that favors filling batches up to a low-latency cap for interactive workloads while allowing longer aggregation when throughput SLOs dominate; 5) Expose new Prometheus metrics: continuous_batcher_queue_wait_seconds_bucket, continuous_batcher_queue_starvation_count, continuous_batcher_dequeue_timeout_count, continuous_batcher_queue_weights; 6) Add end-to-end unit and integration tests plus a micro-benchmark harness used for the perf numbers below. Benchmark summary (internal micro-bench on p3-like nodes, mixed-seq workload): p50 token latency: unchanged (~12ms); p95 token latency: improved from 82ms to 68ms (-17%); p99 token latency: improved from 210ms to 170ms (-19%); tail queue wait (95th of wait time): reduced 3.2x; average batching efficiency: +4% token-per-batch; starvation incidents observed in prior canary windows: 12/24h -> 0/24h after tuning. Configuration and rollout: default config is conservative and preserves prior behavior for existing clusters; new flags continuous_batcher.enable_age_promotion (default true), continuous_batcher.soft_timeout_ms (default 2000), continuous_batcher.max_batch_fill_delay_ms (default 30), continuous_batcher.dynamic_queue_weights_enabled (default true). We will roll out via canary to 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor continuous_batcher_queue_starvation_count, p99 latency, and application-level error rates, then ramp to 25% and 100% if metrics are healthy. Backwards compatibility and failure modes: if dynamic weights cause oscillation under degenerate traffic patterns we fallback to static weights after detection of oscillation using the new metric continuous_batcher_weight_oscillation_detected; in extreme overload we fallback to previous scheduler logic. Tests and validation: added unit tests for age-promotion, timeout eviction, weight adjustment; integration test simulates mixed tenant loads and validates no starvation for 10k simulated requests; benchmark harness reproduces micro-bench numbers and is used in CI benchmark job. Observability: dashboards updated with new panels and an alert continuous-batcher-starvation>0 for 5m. Something-to-note: initial perf CI run reported a small regression in a different bench scenario (highly homogeneous long sequences) which prompted the conservative defaults and the dynamic-toggle, see CI notes below. This PR includes a short rollout playbook in docs/continuous-batcher.md. Related: ENG-4187 describes production incidents and dataset used for benchmarks; ENG-4201 tracks follow-ups for kernel-level improvements tied to dynamic batching. Merge plan: squash and merge after approvals and CI green.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work, can you clarify how age-promotion interacts with priority queues? Are there cases where high-priority low-throughput queues get penalized?

Ava Patel: Age-promotion only increases effective priority for items that have been waiting longer than promotion_threshold_ms; high-priority queues retain absolute priority but promotion ensures low-priority-but-old items eventually get scheduled, comment updated with diagram.
Lina Chen: Please add an integration test for the fallback-to-static-weights behaviour when oscillation is detected.
Ava Patel: Added integration test and a metric to detect oscillation; updated PR description and tests.
